verdicts.reason: A: the headline and body copy run across the teal circle, which has also come loose from the can and drifted to the bottom-left. The CTA has shrunk to a small pill at the top, jammed against the badges, and the brand name now sits below the headline. B: the text is clean and has no collisions, but the can floats away from the circle, the bottom half of the canvas is an arbitrary scatter, and the CTA is still a tiny pill in the top-left, weaker than the badges.

Both put the headline and body copy across the detached circle, put GLACIER below the headline and demote the CTA to a small top-left pill next to the badges. A's body line nearly touches the right edge, its 'BACK BY DEMAND' badge text is tiny, and the SUMMER ONLY pill is misaligned. B is the same layout with slightly better margins.

A keeps the original order (brand, headline, copy, badges, then a prominent dark CTA) on one clean left edge. But the column is stretched apart by large, uneven gaps, and the can sticks out of the top of the circle instead of sitting inside it. B turns the CTA into a small pill stacked with the badges in the top-right corner, which kills its hierarchy. It also moves GLACIER below the headline and leaves a big empty lower-right area.

A has the right hierarchy, a strong CTA button and aligned text, though the vertical spacing is stretched and uneven and the can overhangs the circle. B demotes 'Find It Near You' to a small pill at the same size as the badges, crammed into the top-right corner. It also moves the brand below the headline and leaves the lower-right empty.
